body:
N-34 DESIGN, part 2: the rule that avoids a WRONG album (every claim run on the live code or read in a recorded answer).
A stamp is permanent in effect: refs.find matches deezer_id and isrc first (refs.py:231-236). So the matcher says no readily.
- Step 0, the skip rule: artist and title must survive the fold WHOLE (after NFKD and dropping combining marks every letter/digit is ASCII) and the folded strings must be non-empty and a length known. Proof: two different Fairuz songs both have norm_key '||'; "Habibi"+two different Arabic words both have 'fairuz|habibi|' (so 'non-empty' is NOT enough); "Lukasz" with the slashed L folds to 'ukasz'; Bjork, Beyonce, Sigur Ros pass. Not stored as a miss: asked again when P2-25 lands.
- Step 1: same norm_artist, norm_title AND version_signature. cover_finder.deezer_lookup compares norm_title only (:55) and norm_title strips brackets: 'Comfortably Numb' and 'Comfortably Numb (Live)' are both 'comfortably numb' (signatures {} and {live}).
- Step 2, length: 'Fade Into You (Edit)' (238 s) and 'Fade Into You' (292 s) have the SAME empty signature ('edit' is noise), only the length separates them. 'Hotel California (2013 Remaster)' is the same recording (empty signature).
- Step 3, release: album artist = the song's artist (a feature on someone else's album is a miss: B-118 family); type album/ep before single, unknown values never win (recorded types: album x49, ep x1 in artist_albums.json; no 'compile' seen, so the type does not mark compilations: Legend Remixed and the Legacy sets are 'album'); then the EARLIEST release_date (Comfortably Numb is 382 s on The Wall AND on 'A Foot in the Door: The Best of', only the date tells the original); lowest id last. A lead single comes out before its album, hence album/ep beat single whatever the dates.
- Step 4: the release's track list must hold the hit's id (track_position, disk_number, isrc come from /album/{id}/tracks, not from the search hit, which has only album{id,title,cover_xl}).
- Step 5, pairs: deezer_id/isrc already held by another live ref (unique indexes, 0001_initial.sql:52-54) or another live ref with the same norm_key and release_key(album): HELD, logged, nothing written.
- Length compared: the kept FILE's own length when there is one (N-11 found the import's listing 1 to 12 s off), else ref.duration_ms, else no identity. Tolerance starts at refs.DURATION_TOLERANCE_MS = 3 s, UNMEASURED for YouTube-against-catalogue: the slice 1 dry run prints the histogram over a copy of VM 108's database and the constant is frozen from it. Too tight = misses (asked again by identity_rev); too loose = a permanent wrong id.
- A single is a release of one: its title as the album, track 1, its own folder, ONLY when no album/ep carries the recording (decision 3). Singles/ then means 'no album known'.
- Stored fill-only by refs.release_facts_to_fill: album, track_no, disc_no, year, deezer_id, isrc, cover_url; never title, artists, norm_key or an album an import gave. The 595 '[Unknown Album]' literals become NULL through refs (with touch_ref_holders and touch_file), for every ref the pass examines.
